items.body:
## Summary

fix #28154

This PR fixes a numeric type conversion issue in if-else condition comparison functions. When comparing integer values with float strings (e.g., `0 <= "0.95"`), the code was incorrectly converting float strings to integers, causing precision loss and incorrect evaluation results.

### Changes

- Add `_normalize_numeric_values` function to handle numeric type normalization uniformly
- Refactor numeric comparison functions (greater than, less than, greater than or equal, less than or equal) to use unified type conversion logic
- Fix comparison issues between integers, floats, and string numeric values
- Add unit tests to verify numeric formatting and comparison functionality

### Root Cause

The comparison functions (`_assert_greater_than`, `_assert_less_than`, `_assert_greater_than_or_equal`, `_assert_less_than_or_equal`) in `core/workflow/utils/condition/processor.py` had inconsistent type conversion logic. When comparing `int` values with float strings, the code would convert the string to `int`, losing precision (e.g., `"0.95"` becomes `0`).

### Solution

Introduced a unified `_normalize_numeric_values` function that:
- Converts string numeric values to appropriate numeric types (int or float)
- Preserves precision when comparing integers with float strings
- Handles edge cases properly (e.g., whole number floats converted to ints when comparing with ints)

### Testing

Added comprehensive unit tests in `tests/unit_tests/core/workflow/utils/test_condition.py` covering:
- Integer vs float string comparisons (`0 <= "0.95"`, `1 >= "0.95"`)
- Float vs float string comparisons (`1.1 >= "0.95"`)
- Float vs integer string comparisons (`1.1 > "0"`)

## Screenshots

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| `0 <= "0.95"` evaluates to `False` (incorrect) | `0 <= "0.95"` evaluates to `True` (correct) |
| `1 >= "0.95"` evaluates to `False` (incorrect) | `1 >= "0.95"` evaluates to `True` (correct) |

## Checklist

- [ ] This change requires a documentation update, included: [Dify Document](https://github.com/langgenius/dify-docs)
- [x] I understand that this PR may be closed in case there was no previous discussion or issues. (This doesn't apply to typos!)
- [x] I've added a test for each change that was introduced, and I tried as much as possible to make a single atomic change.
- [x] I've updated the documentation accordingly.
- [x] I ran `dev/reformat`(backend) and `cd web && npx lint-staged`(frontend) to appease the lint gods

items.title: feat: refactor eval sets and improve experiment reporting
items.body:
## What changed - Replace the old eval-set format with YAML tests/locales/assert, plus dataset-level experiments and judge config - Support optional assertions, trusted reference targets, and YAML-defined judge defaults with CLI override precedence - Add richer eval reporting with persisted experimentSummaries, calibrated final scoring, and better aggregate diagnostics - Tighten judge handling with assertion-specific schemas, English rationale instructions, and default judge fallback to OpenAI gpt-5.2 when judge eval is requested - Improve DX with output directory creation, better eval run logging, updated docs, and a sample dataset covering long-form, short UI, and ICU cases ## Checklist - [x] I ran relevant checks locally (`make fmt`, `make lint`, `make test`) - [x] I updated docs, comments, or examples when needed - [x] This PR is scoped and ready for review

Greptile Summary

This PR introduces a significant refactor of the eval pipeline: the dataset format migrates from a flat list to a structured YAML schema (`tests` / `locales` / `assert`), adds dataset-level `experiments` and `judge` config, introduces assertion-specific judge scorers with dedicated prompt templates and parse paths, and adds richer reporting via persisted `experimentSummaries` with calibrated final scoring. The overall architecture is well-designed — strict YAML decoding, thorough dataset validation, idempotent normalization helpers, and a clean scorer interface. The concurrent `execute()` pipeline is correct and the `sanitizeEvalCaseContext` helper is properly isolated. Key issues to resolve before merging: - **Unexpected `llm-rubric` injection** (`service.go`): `normalizedAssertions` defaults to `["llm-rubric"]` when `in.Assertions` is empty, which is then merged with test-level judge assertions in `resolveJudgeScorers` and `aggregateLLMEvaluation`. When a user relies solely on per-test `assert` blocks (without specifying `--assertion` flags or `judge.assertions` in the YAML), an unintended extra `llm-rubric` scorer fires on every run, adding latency and LLM cost and polluting the `LLMEvaluation.Assertions` report field. - **Binary faithfulness score fallback** (`assertion_judge.go`): `parseContextFaithfulnessJudgeResult` defaults the score to 0 when `faithful=true` but `unsupportedClaims` is non-empty — recovering only when the LLM provides an explicit `score` field. If the LLM ever omits `score` while reporting `faithful: true` with minor claims, the result is silently a 0. - **`passCount` fallback inflation** (`cmd/eval.go`): The fallback when `DecisionCounts` is nil uses `SuccessfulRuns` (all error-free runs), not 0 or `DecisionCounts["pass"]`, which would over-report the pass rate column. - **Generated artifact committed without gitignore** (`artifacts/article_001_report.json`): The 2720-line generated report is not gitignored and will bloat the repo on future runs.

Confidence Score: 3/5

- Not safe to merge as-is — two logic issues (unexpected default scorer injection, binary faithfulness fallback) can produce incorrect evaluation results and inflated API costs. - The core refactor is solid and the architecture is sound, but the `normalizedAssertions` default injection into `resolveJudgeScorers` is a real behavioral bug that silently changes what evaluations run. Combined with the binary faithfulness fallback and the pass-rate overcounting, there are enough logic-level concerns to hold the PR for fixes. - `internal/i18n/evalsvc/service.go` (normalizedAssertions default), `internal/i18n/evalsvc/assertion_judge.go` (parseContextFaithfulnessJudgeResult score fallback), and `cmd/eval.go` (passCount fallback + double Validate).

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | internal/i18n/evalsvc/service.go | Core orchestration file with the most significant issue: `normalizedAssertions` injects `llm-rubric` as an implicit default whenever `in.Assertions` is empty, which causes an unintended extra judge call when test-level assertions have already determined the required scorers. Also contains well-structured aggregation logic for runs, cases, and experiments. | | internal/i18n/evalsvc/assertion_judge.go | New file defining assertion-specific judge scorers and their prompt templates; contains a fragile binary score fallback in `parseContextFaithfulnessJudgeResult` that collapses to 0 when `faithful=true` but any `unsupportedClaims` are present, relying entirely on the LLM always providing an explicit `score` field to recover. | | cmd/eval.go | CLI command layer refactored to use `ExperimentSummaries` for output; has a semantic bug in the `passCount` fallback (uses `SuccessfulRuns` instead of 0 when `DecisionCounts` is nil), and performs a redundant `input.Validate()` call before forwarding to `evalsvc.Run`. | | internal/i18n/evalset/types.go | New YAML schema defining Dataset, Test, Vars, LocaleTarget, Assertion, and Case types; validation logic is thorough with duplicate-ID checks, assertion type validation, and threshold range checks. The `normalizeAssertionType` / `judgeAssertionType` dual normalization is complex but consistent. | | internal/i18n/evalset/load.go | Simple, clean loader using strict YAML decoding with `KnownFields(true)`; correctly delegates to `Dataset.Validate()` before returning. | | internal/i18n/evalsvc/llm_judge.go | Refactored to add an `effectiveLLMJudgePrompt` helper that appends JSON-format and English-rationale instructions to any custom prompt; parse helpers (rubric, payload, dimensions) are well-structured with good error handling. | | internal/i18n/evalsvc/scoring/evaluator.go | Evaluator unchanged from a structural standpoint; hard-fail set logic and weighted aggregate computation look correct; `dedupAdjacent` relies on sorted input which is correctly ensured upstream. | | artifacts/article_001_report.json | 2720-line generated eval report committed to the repository without a corresponding `.gitignore` entry; will bloat the repo and cause merge conflicts on subsequent eval runs. | | eval_dataset/article_001.yaml | Well-structured sample dataset covering long-form article, short UI strings, and ICU plural cases; correctly uses dataset-level `judge` config and per-experiment IDs. |

Sequence Diagram

 ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant CLI as cmd/eval.go participant Svc as evalsvc.Service participant Loader as evalset.Load participant Workers as execute() workers participant Judge as AssertionJudgeScorer participant Translator as translator.Translate CLI->>CLI: input.Validate() (1st call) CLI->>Svc: Run(ctx, input) Svc->>Svc: in.Validate() (2nd call – redundant) Svc->>Loader: Load(evalSetPath) Loader-->>Svc: Dataset (experiments, judge, cases) Svc->>Svc: normalizeEvalInput(in, dataset) Note over Svc: Inherits judge.provider/model/assertions
Falls back to gpt-5.2 if eval requested Svc->>Svc: resolveJudgeScorers(in, cases) Note over Svc: ⚠️ normalizedAssertions([]) → ["llm-rubric"]
merged with requiredJudgeAssertions(cases)
→ injects llm-rubric even when not requested Svc->>Workers: execute(cases × experiments) loop For each case × experiment Workers->>Translator: Translate(req) Translator-->>Workers: translated text Workers->>Judge: ScoreJudge(scoreInput) Judge->>Translator: LLM judge call Translator-->>Judge: JSON response Judge-->>Workers: JudgeResult Workers->>Workers: evaluateAssertions() Workers->>Workers: finalizeRun() → calibratedFinalScore + classifyRunDecision end Workers-->>Svc: []RunResult Svc->>Svc: aggregateRuns / summarizeCases / summarizeExperiments Svc->>Svc: aggregateLLMEvaluation Note over Svc: ⚠️ Same default injection in Assertions list Svc-->>CLI: Report CLI->>CLI: writeExperimentSummary(ExperimentSummaries) ```

Comments Outside Diff (6)

 1. `internal/i18n/evalsvc/service.go`, line 3711 ([link](https://github.com/quiet-circles/hyperlocalise/blob/036308889c5218b934aa1861f396305a8090eb4d/internal/i18n/evalsvc/service.go#L3711)) **Nil pointer dereference after nil guard** `normalizeEvalInput` guards `if dataset != nil` for the first block but then unconditionally calls `dataset.Cases` on the very next statement. If `dataset` is `nil` (which the guard explicitly acknowledges as a possible value), this will panic at runtime. ```go if !evalRequested(in, dataset.Cases) { // panics if dataset is nil ``` The fix is to pass a nil-safe slice: The `Run()` caller always passes a non-nil `dataset` today, but the presence of the nil guard combined with the unchecked access is a latent panic waiting for any future caller that passes `nil`. 2. `cmd/eval_test.go`, line 352-357 ([link](https://github.com/quiet-circles/hyperlocalise/blob/036308889c5218b934aa1861f396305a8090eb4d/cmd/eval_test.go#L352-L357)) **Log messages written to stderr will never appear in `out` (stdout buffer)** `logEvalRunStart` and `logEvalRunComplete` both write to `cmd.ErrOrStderr()`, but the test only wires `cmd.SetOut(&out)` — it never calls `cmd.SetErr(&out)`. In Cobra, `OutOrStdout()` and `ErrOrStderr()` are completely independent writers; setting one has no effect on the other. Because `SetErr` is not called, `ErrOrStderr()` falls back to `os.Stderr`, so the `"eval: starting …"` and `"eval: judge …"` strings will never land in `out`. These two assertions will always fail: ```go // "eval: starting …" → written to os.Stderr, not to out if !strings.Contains(out.String(), "eval: starting dataset=set.json") { … } // "eval: judge …" → same if !strings.Contains(out.String(), "eval: judge provider=openai …") { … } ``` Fix by capturing stderr in a separate buffer and asserting against it: ```go var out, errOut bytes.Buffer cmd.SetOut(&out) cmd.SetErr(&errOut) // ... execute ... if !strings.Contains(errOut.String(), "eval: starting dataset=set.json") { t.Fatalf("expected start log, got %q", errOut.String()) } if !strings.Contains(errOut.String(), "eval: judge provider=openai model=gpt-5.2 assertions=llm-rubric") { t.Fatalf("expected judge log, got %q", errOut.String()) } ``` 3. `internal/i18n/evalsvc/scoring/evaluator.go`, line 3058-3095 ([link](https://github.com/quiet-circles/hyperlocalise/blob/036308889c5218b934aa1861f396305a8090eb4d/internal/i18n/evalsvc/scoring/evaluator.go#L3058-L3095)) **`LengthCompliance` and `TermCompliance` always return `1.0` — tags are never passed in** The new `Case` struct (in `types.go`) has no `Tags` field — tags were part of the old CSV format and were not ported to the YAML format. As a result, every call site passes `nil` for the `tags` parameter: ```go run.Quality = s.qualityEvaluator.Evaluate(tc.Source, translated, tc.Reference, tc.TargetLocale, nil) ``` This means: - `lengthComplianceScore` always returns `1.0` (early-exits because `hasTag(nil, "ui")` is `false`) - `termComplianceScore` always returns `1.0` (no `"forbidden:"` tags to match) Both dimensions therefore contribute a constant perfect score to the `WeightedAggregate`, inflating scores regardless of actual translation quality. The corresponding hard-fail constants (`HardFailLengthOutOfBound`, `HardFailForbiddenTerms`) can never be triggered through the current flow. The weight allocation (`LengthCompliance: 0.1`, `TermCompliance: 0.05`) artificially accounts for 15 % of the heuristic denominator with invariant values. Consider either: - adding a `Tags []string` field to `evalset.Case` and populating it from the YAML (e.g. from `vars` or a new `tags` field), or - removing these checks from the weight formula and deferring them until tags are surfaced. 4. `internal/i18n/evalsvc/service.go`, line 4177-4184 ([link](https://github.com/quiet-circles/hyperlocalise/blob/036308889c5218b934aa1861f396305a8090eb4d/internal/i18n/evalsvc/service.go#L4177-L4184)) **Assertion errors treated the same as assertion failures, masking judge-lane outages** `hasAssertionFailures` returns `true` for both a failed assertion (`!result.Passed`) and an assertion *error* (e.g. `"required judge result missing"`, `"judge returned no score"`). Both paths flow into `calibratedFinalScore` → `finalScore = 0` and `classifyRunDecision` → `"fail"`. An error in the judge lane (network failure, model timeout, schema mismatch) is qualitatively different from a deliberate assertion failure. Treating them identically means a transient judge outage silently converts every run to `decision=fail` and `finalScore=0`, which will break CI gates and make regressions hard to distinguish from infrastructure problems. Consider separating the two: ```go func hasAssertionFailures(results []AssertionResult) bool { for _, result := range results { if !result.Passed && strings.TrimSpace(result.Error) == "" { return true // deterministic failure, not an error } } return false } ``` Errors could be surfaced via a separate `hasAssertionErrors` check and handled by elevating the run to `"review"` rather than `"fail"`. 2. `internal/i18n/evalsvc/service.go`, line 928-937 ([link](https://github.com/quiet-circles/hyperlocalise/blob/9f0a7e290cfb4210c70edcc78541578a7aea9926/internal/i18n/evalsvc/service.go#L928-L937)) **Unexpected `llm-rubric` injection when only test-level assertions are present** `normalizedAssertions` unconditionally returns `["llm-rubric"]` when `in.Assertions` is empty. This is then merged with `requiredJudgeAssertions(cases)` inside `resolveJudgeScorers` (and again in `aggregateLLMEvaluation`). The problematic scenario: - User runs `eval run --eval-set dataset.yaml` with **no** `--assertion` flags - Dataset has **no** `judge.assertions` - Individual tests have `assert: [{type: context-faithfulness, threshold: 0.8}]` In this case, `normalizedAssertions([])` → `["llm-rubric"]` and `requiredJudgeAssertions(cases)` → `["context-faithfulness"]`. The merge produces `["context-faithfulness", "llm-rubric"]`, silently adding an extra `llm-rubric` scorer that was never requested. This runs an additional LLM API call per test case and incorrectly lists `llm-rubric` in the `LLMEvaluation.Assertions` field of the report. The intent of the default (`"llm-rubric"` when nothing is specified) seems appropriate when LLM eval is requested via `--eval-provider`/`--eval-model` with no assertions. But when test-level assertions have already determined which judges are needed, the default should not be injected. ```go // In resolveJudgeScorers, consider only injecting the default when there // are no required test-level assertions to fall back on: required := requiredJudgeAssertions(cases) if len(required) == 0 { required = normalizedAssertions(in.Assertions) } else { // merge explicitly-requested CLI assertions (without injecting defaults) cliAssertions := canonicalJudgeAssertions(in.Assertions) required = mergeAssertionKinds(cliAssertions, required) } ``` The same pattern should be applied consistently in `aggregateLLMEvaluation` at line 613. 3. `internal/i18n/evalsvc/assertion_judge.go`, line 412-420 ([link](https://github.com/quiet-circles/hyperlocalise/blob/9f0a7e290cfb4210c70edcc78541578a7aea9926/internal/i18n/evalsvc/assertion_judge.go#L412-L420)) **Binary score fallback produces 0 when `faithful=true` but claims are non-empty** The computed default score is 1 only when `faithful && len(unsupportedClaims) == 0`. When `faithful=true` but the LLM also lists some `unsupportedClaims` (e.g. minor issues), the computed score defaults to 0 — which is then overridden by the explicit `score` field if the LLM includes it. In practice the LLM is always instructed to return a `score` field (see `contextFaithfulnessTemplate`), so this is typically overridden correctly. However, if the LLM ever omits the `score` field (malformed response that still parses), a translation the LLM judged as `faithful` would receive a score of 0 silently. This is misleading during debugging and fragile under partial LLM compliance. The real-world artifact data confirms this pattern: multiple runs show `"faithful": true` with a non-empty `unsupportedClaims` list and an explicit score of 0.90–0.97 — the only thing preventing a false-zero is the explicit score override. A more robust fallback would derive a proportional score from the claim count rather than hard-coding 0: ```go score := 0.0 if faithful { // Graceful degradation: penalise per unsupported claim rather than // collapsing to 0 as soon as any minor claim is flagged. score = math.Max(0, 1.0-float64(len(unsupportedClaims))*0.1) } ``` 4. `cmd/eval.go`, line 271-278 ([link](https://github.com/quiet-circles/hyperlocalise/blob/9f0a7e290cfb4210c70edcc78541578a7aea9926/cmd/eval.go#L271-L278)) **`passCount` fallback inflates reported pass rate** When `DecisionCounts` is nil, `passCount` defaults to `summary.SuccessfulRuns`. However, `SuccessfulRuns` counts runs that did not produce a translation error — it includes runs whose decision was `"review"` or `"fail"`. This means the fallback path would report all non-error runs as passing, which is semantically wrong. In practice `DecisionCounts` is always non-nil for summaries derived from real runs (since `finalizeRun` always sets a decision), but the fallback would silently produce inflated numbers if the summary is reconstructed from an older report format or zero-value data. 5. `cmd/eval.go`, line 86-88 ([link](https://github.com/quiet-circles/hyperlocalise/blob/9f0a7e290cfb4210c70edcc78541578a7aea9926/cmd/eval.go#L86-L88)) **Redundant `input.Validate()` call** `input.Validate()` is called here and then called a second time unconditionally inside `evalsvc.Service.Run()` (line 262 of `service.go`), before any normalization. Since `Validate` is idempotent and has no side effects, this is harmless, but it's redundant work. Consider removing the explicit call here and relying on the one inside `evalsvc.Run`, which is the authoritative validation gate — especially since normalization (`normalizeEvalInput`) happens inside `Service.Run` and could change the shape of assertions before the second validation fires anyway. Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time! 6. `artifacts/article_001_report.json`, line 1 ([link](https://github.com/quiet-circles/hyperlocalise/blob/9f0a7e290cfb4210c70edcc78541578a7aea9926/artifacts/article_001_report.json#L1)) **Generated artifact committed without a gitignore entry** `artifacts/article_001_report.json` is a 2720-line generated JSON report. Committing generated eval output to the repo will: - Bloat the repository on every eval run committed - Cause noisy merge conflicts when different developers regenerate reports - Mix generated data with source-controlled code The `.gitignore` currently has no entry for the `artifacts/` directory. Consider either removing this file from the PR and adding `artifacts/` (or `artifacts/*.json`) to `.gitignore`, or moving sample reports to a documentation-only directory that is explicitly tracked and not regenerated automatically.

## Summary

- Add `full_techniques` branch in `save_evaluation_results()` to convert BMAD category scores to `sommelier_outputs` format

## Problem

When running 75-technique evaluation mode (`full_techniques`), all results were incorrectly displayed as "Jean-Pierre" / "Final Synthesis" because:

1. **Backend**: `save_evaluation_results()` had no handling for `full_techniques` mode - it fell through to `six_sommeliers` logic which found no results
2. **Frontend**: `getSommelierTheme()` returned `jeanpierre` as fallback when IDs didn't match any defined sommelier

## Solution

1. **Backend** (`evaluation_service.py`):
   - Added `elif is_full_techniques:` branch to handle BMAD category scores
   - Converts 4 BMAD categories (A: Problem Definition, B: Technical Design, C: Implementation, D: Documentation) to `sommelier_outputs` format
   - Scales raw scores to 0-100 range

2. **Frontend** (`sommeliers.ts`):
   - Added 4 new sommelier themes for BMAD categories with appropriate colors and images

3. **Frontend** (`api.ts`):
   - Added SOMMELIER_ROLES mapping for the new category names

## Files Changed

- `backend/app/services/evaluation_service.py` - Added full_techniques result handling
- `frontend/src/lib/sommeliers.ts` - Added BMAD category themes
- `frontend/src/lib/api.ts` - Added role mappings

items.title: prithvi has been nominated and accepted for maintainership
items.body:
### Description

I’d like to nominate Prithvi(iprithv) as a maintainer of the dashboards-search-relevance repository.
Prithvi has been actively contributing to the Search Relevance Dashboard for over five months. His contributions began with augmenting the filtering capabilities in the Dashboard UI for finding search configurations, query sets, and judgements, followed by several bug fixes and enhancements. More recently, he played a key role in building out more ways for users to interact with SRW datasets, including manual editing and upload capabilities.

He lately has been polishing up lots of small issues in the UI, like missing cron expression in scheduling experiments.   Longer term he has some early draft PR’s around integrating a rich code editor for the Query DSL in the SRW UI, and expanding more into the backend work as well.

Prithvi got involved in OpenSearch after building a RAG help desk system for his firm.  His firm views OpenSearch as a key technology and has been supportive of his involvement.   He has been a regular member of the Wednesday Search Triage meeting on Zoom as well as meeting with me 1 on 1 every week to sync on contributions.

Prithvi will continue maintaining and contributing to the dashboards-search-relevance repo, and has also been actively involved in reviewing pull requests across the project.

Here are a few examples of his work specific to the dashboards repo (not including his backend contributions:

Evaluation Workflow & UX Improvements
These changes transformed the workflow from rigid batch experimentation into an iterative debugging tool for relevance engineers.

- Single Query Comparison Execution (https://github.com/opensearch-project/dashboards-search-relevance/pull/746)
He introduced the ability to run experiments on a single query instead of full datasets, significantly reducing iteration cycles and enabling interactive debugging of ranking behaviour. His change allowed faster experimentation loops.

- Reuse Search Configurations (https://github.com/opensearch-project/dashboards-search-relevance/pull/727)
He enabled reuse of search configurations, removing repetitive setup work and allowing systematic tuning workflows in production experimentation environments. This reduced friction in daily usage.

- Manual Query Set Creation (https://github.com/opensearch-project/dashboards-search-relevance/pull/754)
He implemented manual dataset authoring directly in the UI, making the feature usable without external dataset preparation and improving adoption by new users. His implementation lowered onboarding barriers.

- Judgment Detail UX Improvements (https://github.com/opensearch-project/dashboards-search-relevance/pull/713)
He simplified the rating workflow, reducing cognitive load and improving evaluator efficiency.

Correctness & Data Safety Fixes
These fixes prevent invalid evaluation conclusions, a critical responsibility in relevance tooling.

- Deleting Judgment Ratings Bug (https://github.com/opensearch-project/dashboards-search-relevance/pull/751)
He fixed a bug that could cause rating associations to be lost, protecting experiment validity and preventing silent incorrect results. His fix safeguarded evaluation reliability.

- Single Query Comparison UI Misalignment (https://github.com/opensearch-project/dashboards-search-relevance/pull/752)
He corrected a UI mismatch that could lead users to misinterpret evaluation results.

- GUID Filtering for Judgments & Query Sets (https://github.com/opensearch-project/dashboards-search-relevance/pull/689, https://github.com/opensearch-project/dashboards-search-relevance/pull/687)
He added precise dataset filtering, enabling large‑scale dataset management in enterprise scenarios.
### Issues Resolved


### Check List

items.title: add event attributes
items.body:
## Pull Request

### Short Summary

Completes OTel GenAI semantic convention coverage started in #263 by adding 14 missing span attributes and full event extraction. `GenAiSpanRecord` now captures `gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details` events (opt-in content: input/output messages, system instructions, tool definitions) and `gen_ai.evaluation.result` events (eval scores, labels, explanations). The genai Delta Lake schema grows by 15 columns to match.

### Context

PR #263 extracted the core scalar attributes from GenAI spans. It did not handle:

1. **14 missing span attributes** — `gen_ai.agent.description`, `gen_ai.agent.version`, `gen_ai.data_source.id`, `gen_ai.request.choice.count`, `gen_ai.request.seed`, `gen_ai.request.frequency_penalty`, `gen_ai.request.presence_penalty`, `gen_ai.request.stop_sequences`, `server.address`, `server.port`, plus the four opt-in content fields (`gen_ai.input.messages`, `gen_ai.output.messages`, `gen_ai.system_instructions`, `gen_ai.tool.definitions`).

2. **OTel event extraction** — The spec defines two event types that carry data no span attribute can express. `gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details` is the event counterpart to an inference span — it carries the full scalar set plus opt-in content, so instrumentation libraries can emit it standalone (no span context required). `gen_ai.evaluation.result` carries eval scores attached to a span; there is no span attribute equivalent.

**Source-of-truth rule** — this is worth understanding before reviewing:

```
Scalar attrs (tokens, model, operation, finish_reasons, etc.)
  → span attributes only, no event fallback

Opt-in content (input_messages, output_messages, system_instructions, tool_definitions)
  → span attribute first; falls back to gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details event

gen_ai.evaluation.result
  → events only
```

The first group is intentional: scalar metrics queries (token counts, model breakdown, agent activity) must not silently switch data sources mid-query. The event duplicates span scalars for the standalone case; when both are present, span wins.

**eval_results storage** — `Vec<GenAiEvalResult>` is JSON-serialized and stored as `Utf8View` in Delta Lake. This avoids a nested list column (which DataFusion handles less cleanly for nullable struct arrays) at the cost of a `serde_json::from_str` on read. Acceptable here because eval events are uncommon and the field is only materialized when the column is non-null.

**Schema evolution** — 15 new nullable columns are appended to the genai Delta Lake schema. Delta Lake handles nullable column additions without breaking existing Parquet files; DataFusion projects the schema and fills NULLs for rows in older files.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `crates/scouter_types/src/trace/genai.rs` | 14 new span attribute constants, 4 opt-in content constants, 2 event name constants, 4 eval attribute constants, `GenAiEvalResult` struct, 14 new fields on `GenAiSpanRecord`, `extract_gen_ai_events()`, event merge in `extract_gen_ai_span()` |
| `crates/scouter_types/src/trace/mod.rs` | `GenAiEvalResult` added to pub re-exports |
| `crates/scouter_dataframe/src/parquet/tracing/genai.rs` | 15 new column constants, 15 Arrow schema fields, 15 batch builder fields + init + append + finish, `batches_to_genai_records()` extraction for all 15 |
| `py-scouter/docs/docs/tracing/genai-semantics.md` | Rewrote the span events section (previously said events were not extracted — now incorrect), added opt-in content section, added evaluation results section, expanded attribute table with all new fields |
| `py-scouter/mkdocs.yml` | Nav entry for genai-semantics doc |
| `.github/workflows/publish-docs.yml` | Add Rust toolchain install step to docs CI |

### Is this a Breaking Change?

No for any caller that did not write genai spans between the merge of #263 and this PR. The 15 new columns are nullable — Delta Lake schema evolution fills them as NULL for rows in older files, so DataFusion queries and `batches_to_genai_records()` both handle missing data correctly. If genai span data was written between #263 and this PR, those files will read back with NULLs in the new columns rather than failing.

`GenAiSpanRecord` gains 14 new fields but derives `Default`, so any code constructing one via struct literal will get a compile error prompting the update. No HTTP API or serialization contract changes.

(use the c.x branch) | ❌ | Automated tests included? | ✔️ | Related user documentation PR URL | mautic/user-documentation#... | Related developer documentation PR URL | mautic/developer-documentation-new#... | Issue(s) addressed | Fixes #... ## Description Segment date filters do not work properly after switching the configuration to another language. #### Current behavior * When switching **from English to another language (e.g. German)**: * A relative date like `today` is persisted as a localized date string instead of remaining relative. * When switching **from another language (e.g. German) back to English**: * A relative value such as `heute` gets converted to `1970-01-01 00:00`. This breaks segment evaluation, leading to incorrect results when running segment updates. #### Proposed solution * Store **relative date values in English** in the database. * Translate these values **only at the UI level**, based on the currently selected language. This ensures: * Consistent and stable persistence. * Correct evaluation regardless of language changes. * Proper localization without affecting stored data. #### Related work This PR is conceptually similar to [https://github.com/mautic/mautic/pull/10541](https://github.com/mautic/mautic/pull/10541), but extends the approach by allowing **relative date strings to be displayed in multiple languages**, rather than being locked to a single locale. This PR is a port of https://github.com/mautic/mautic/pull/12411. The original PR introduced the approach of storing relative date values in English and translating them at the UI layer. This port adapts the same logic for the current target branch while preserving the original behavior and intent. --- ### 📋 Steps to test this PR: 1. Open this PR on Gitpod or pull down for testing locally (see docs on testing PRs [here](https://contribute.mautic.org/contributing-to-mautic/tester)) 2. Set **English** as the current language. 3. Create a new segment. 4. Add a date-based filter and set a relative value (e.g., *Date Last Active equals today*). 4. Save the segment. 5. Switch the language to **German**. 6. Verify the relative value is translated correctly (e.g., `heute`). 7. Create another new segment 8. Add a date-based filter using a relative value in German (e.g. *Letzte Aktivität Datum gleich heute*). 8. Save the segment. 9. Switch the language back to **English**. 10. Verify the relative value is translated correctly (e.g., `today`). 11. Run `mautic:segment:update` and confirm it executes successfully.

items.title: [EL] DEBUG-4879 Support multiple expression compilations

labels.name: area:tracer
labels.description: The core tracer library (Datadog.Trace, does not include OpenTracing, native code, or integrations)

items.body:
## Summary of changes
- Reworked `ProbeExpressionEvaluator` to cache compiled expressions **per runtime type combination** (invocation target, return value, and scope members), instead of a single `Lazy<>` instance shared across all invocations.
- Introduced `ExpressionCacheKey` to uniquely identify a compilation context using **runtime types** (`Value.GetType()` when available) and member runtime types to support polymorphic calls.
- Replaced single cached fields with `ConcurrentDictionary<ExpressionCacheKey, …>` caches for:
  - Templates (`CompiledExpression<string>[]?`)
  - Condition (`CompiledExpression<bool>?`)
  - Metric (`CompiledExpression<double>?`)
  - Span decorations (compiled decorations array)
- Preserved evaluation semantics and error aggregation, while ensuring compiled delegates match the actual runtime types.

## Reason for change
The previous implementation compiled expressions once (on first invocation) and reused them for all subsequent calls. This fails in polymorphic scenarios where:
- The declared type differs from the runtime type (e.g., generics/base class/interface method invoked on a derived instance).
- Parameters/locals are declared as a base type (or `object`) but carry different concrete runtime types across invocations.

In these cases, delegates compiled against the first observed type can fail later (typically invalid casts / expression binding mismatches), causing evaluation errors and incorrect probe results.

## Implementation details
- Compute a **runtime-aware cache key** on each `Evaluate()` call:
  - `thisType`: `InvocationTarget.Value?.GetType()` (fallback to declared type, then `typeof(object)`)
  - `returnType`: `Return.Value?.GetType()` (fallback to declared type)
  - `members`: runtime types captured from `ScopeMember.Value?.GetType()` (fallback to declared `ScopeMember.Type`)
- Store compiled artifacts in thread-safe caches:
  - `ConcurrentDictionary<ExpressionCacheKey, ...>`
  - On cache miss: compile, then `TryAdd`
- Added `ExpressionCacheKey` struct:
  - Precomputes hash over `thisType`, `returnType`, and member runtime types.
  - Implements equality by comparing `ThisType`, `ReturnType`, and the captured member type sequence (hash used as a fast-path).
- Added debug logging for cache misses (type + hash + cache size) to help diagnose compilation churn and verify caching behavior.

## Test coverage
- Existing `DebuggerExpressionLanguageTests` remain supported via `CompiledTemplates` / `CompiledCondition` accessors (now returning the first cached entry).
- Snapshot Exploration Test

## Dependencies
- Depends on: #7991, #7992, #7993
- Merge order: #7991 → #7992 → #7993 → (this PR)

## Other details
- Caches may grow with many unique type combinations; however this is required for correctness under polymorphic workloads. If needed later, we can add eviction/size caps.
- This PR is part of an effort to make the Snapshot Exploration Test run successfully end-to-end.

items.title: [BUG] `BaseGridSearch`: Ensure censoring data (C) is passed in all refit loops

labels.name: module:regression
labels.description: probabilistic regression module

items.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a refit inconsistency in `BaseGridSearch._fit_best` inside:

```
skpro/model_selection/_tuning.py
```

During refitting:

* `best_estimator_` was correctly refit using:

```python
estimator.fit(X, y, C=C)
```

* However, estimators stored in `n_best_estimators_` were refit using:

```python
estimator.fit(X, y)
```

This caused survival estimators inside `n_best_estimators_` to be refit **without censoring information**, producing silently incorrect models.

This PR ensures that censoring data (`C`) is forwarded consistently across all refit paths.

The fix applies to both:

* `GridSearchCV`
* `RandomizedSearchCV`

since both rely on `BaseGridSearch._fit_best`.

---

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a survival estimator that requires censoring data.
2. Run grid search with multiple returned estimators:

```python
gscv = GridSearchCV(
    estimator=survival_estimator,
    param_grid=...,
    return_n_best_estimators=2
)

gscv.fit(X, y, C=C)
```

3. Inspect:

   * `gscv.best_estimator_`
   * `gscv.n_best_estimators_[0][1]`

### Before Fix

* `best_estimator_` receives `C`
* `n_best_estimators_` models are refit **without `C`**
* No error is raised
* Predictions may differ silently due to missing censoring information

---

## Impact

This bug affects survival workflows where censoring data is required for correct likelihood estimation.

Consequences:

* Models in `n_best_estimators_` are incorrectly trained
* Downstream evaluation or ensembling may produce inconsistent results
* No exception is raised → silent correctness issue

This is particularly problematic in research or benchmarking scenarios where multiple top models are compared.

---

## Fix

The refit loop in `_fit_best` has been aligned so that all estimators receive `C`.

### Before

```python
if self.refit:
    estimator.fit(X, y)
```

### After

```python
if self.refit:
    # Pass C so survival estimators receive censoring data,
    # matching the best_estimator_ refit above
    estimator.fit(X, y, C=C)
```

This ensures:

* `best_estimator_`
* All entries in `n_best_estimators_`

are refit consistently with censoring data.

The change is localized and does not alter behavior for non-survival estimators.

---

## Result

After this fix:

* Refit behavior is consistent across all returned estimators
* Survival estimators always receive censoring data
* No silent loss of censoring information
* Behavior between `best_estimator_` and `n_best_estimators_` is now aligned

All existing tests pass, and no new dependencies were introduced.

---

## What reviewers should focus on

* Consistency between refit paths
* Correct forwarding of optional `C`
* Confirmation that `RandomizedSearchCV` is also covered
* No behavioral change for estimators that do not use `C`

items.title: Fix history message ordering in evaluation bot generation
items.body:
This is Cloud AI Generated and not tested, submitting in case its accurate:

## Problem

When running evaluations with the generation step enabled, conversation history was not being properly included in the bot's context. This resulted in the bot not seeing previous messages in the conversation, leading to incorrect or inconsistent evaluation results.

### Root Cause

The bug was introduced in the initial evaluation system implementation (commit ad52ac5, Oct 14, 2025) but only became active when history population was added in commit 63f7b7b (Oct 7, 2025).

When populating chat history for evaluation sessions in `apps/evaluations/tasks.py:113-127`, the code used `ChatMessage.objects.bulk_create()` to create multiple history messages at once:

```python
history_messages = [
    ChatMessage(
        chat=chat,
        message_type=history_entry.get("message_type", ChatMessageType.HUMAN),
        content=history_entry.get("content", ""),
        summary=history_entry.get("summary"),
    )
    for history_entry in message.history
]
ChatMessage.objects.bulk_create(history_messages)
```

**The Issue**: Since `ChatMessage.created_at` has `auto_now_add=True`, all messages created in the same `bulk_create()` call receive identical timestamps (or timestamps within microseconds of each other).

Later, when the LLM node retrieves history using `chat.messages.order_by("created_at")` (in `apps/chat/models.py:69` and `apps/chat/conversation.py:124`), messages with identical timestamps have **undefined ordering** in SQL. The database may return them in any order, often based on primary key or internal row ordering, which is not guaranteed to match the original chronological sequence.

### Impact

- History messages appear in random or incorrect order
- The bot receives scrambled conversation context
- Evaluation results are unreliable because the bot doesn't see the proper conversation flow
- This affects all evaluations using the generation step with multi-turn conversations

## Solution

Set explicit `created_at` timestamps with 1-second increments for each history message to ensure proper chronological ordering:

```python
base_time = timezone.now() - timedelta(seconds=len(message.history))
history_messages = [
    ChatMessage(
        chat=chat,
        message_type=history_entry.get("message_type", ChatMessageType.HUMAN),
        content=history_entry.get("content", ""),
        summary=history_entry.get("summary"),
        created_at=base_time + timedelta(seconds=idx),  # Explicit timestamp
    )
    for idx, history_entry in enumerate(message.history)
]
```

This ensures that:
1. Each message has a unique timestamp
2. Messages maintain chronological order when retrieved with `order_by("created_at")`
3. The bot receives history in the correct sequence

## Testing

Manual testing should verify:
- [ ] Run an evaluation with generation enabled on a dataset with multi-turn conversations
- [ ] Verify that the bot's responses consider previous conversation context
- [ ] Check that history messages appear in correct order in the session chat

Existing tests pass:
- `apps/evaluations/tests/test_evaluation_tasks.py::test_run_bot_generation` - Verifies basic bot generation
- `apps/evaluations/tests/test_evaluation_tasks.py::test_run_bot_generation_with_participant_data_session_state` - Verifies context passing

## Why This Wasn't Caught Earlier

The bug was latent in the codebase:
- The history handling code existed since Oct 14, 2025 (ad52ac5)
- History population was added Oct 7, 2025 (63f7b7b)
- The bug only manifested when history was actually populated
- Inconsistent ordering might have appeared correct "most of the time" depending on database internals and primary key ordering coincidentally matching chronological order

## Files Changed

- `apps/evaluations/tasks.py` - Fixed timestamp assignment in `run_bot_generation()`

items.title: Comprehensively harden signal pipeline, async lifecycle, caching, and tests
items.body:
This PR addresses the current review findings across the signal pipeline: confidence mutations in `Scanner` were being overwritten, router delivery state could drift from actual Telegram sends, fallback/cache behavior was ambiguous under degradation, and WebSocket/AI/OpenAI lifecycle handling had correctness gaps. The changes focus on making state transitions explicit, preserving confidence adjustments in the intended order, and extending behavioral coverage around the failure paths that matter.

- **Scanner confidence pipeline and structure**
  - Refactors `Scanner._scan_symbol()` into smaller internal helpers for context building, gating, confidence computation, external enrichments, and enqueueing.
  - Reorders confidence handling so adjustments are applied cumulatively instead of being lost:
    - base confidence
    - regime/channel adjustments
    - predictive adjustments
    - OpenAI adjustments
    - final clamp + threshold check
  - Preserves existing scan behavior while making control flow easier to debug and test.

  ```python
  sig.confidence = base_confidence
  self._apply_regime_channel_adjustments(...)
  await self._apply_predictive_adjustments(...)
  if not await self._apply_openai_adjustments(...):
      return None
  sig.confidence = self._clamp_confidence(sig.confidence)
  if sig.confidence < min_conf:
      return None
  ```

- **Router delivery correctness and free-limit handling**
  - Changes `SignalRouter` to mark signals active only after a confirmed successful Telegram send.
  - Respects `send_message()` return values; failed/non-confirmed sends no longer leave stale active signals or position locks behind.
  - Fixes free-channel limit handling so `0` is treated as a real limit rather than being coerced into retaining one item.

- **Queue overflow and degradation semantics**
  - Makes Redis fallback behavior explicit across `redis_client`, `signal_queue`, and `state_cache`: Redis operation failures now switch the system into in-memory mode instead of continuing in an ambiguous mixed state.
  - Adds queue overflow telemetry/tracking (`dropped_signals`, `overflow_events`, last dropped id) and a hook for repeated-drop admin alerts.
  - Makes in-memory `StateCache` TTL behavior predictable by enforcing expiry locally as well.

- **WebSocket lifecycle, health, and fallback bookkeeping**
  - Makes shutdown deterministic by cancelling and awaiting watchdog, fallback, and connection tasks.
  - Fixes health reporting so disconnected/closed connection sets are not reported healthy.
  - Tracks degradation per connection so fallback remains active until all degraded critical streams recover, rather than disabling on the first recovery.

- **AI engine session/cache lifecycle**
  - Adds cache pruning to prevent stale/unbounded module-level cache growth.
  - Reuses a shared `aiohttp` session for AI fetches when a session is not supplied, reducing avoidable session churn while keeping graceful degradation behavior intact.

- **OpenAI evaluator cache and parsing correctness**
  - Replaces the coarse `symbol:channel` cache key with a fingerprint of the meaningful evaluation inputs so distinct signal contexts do not incorrectly share cached results.
  - Hardens parsing for model responses that include fenced JSON or extra wrapper text.
  - Reduces risky/noisy API error logging by avoiding large response-body logging on failures.

- **Test coverage updates**
  - Extends scanner tests to prove confidence adjustments persist and OpenAI skip behavior blocks enqueueing.
  - Adds router tests for failed delivery and real zero free-limit behavior.
  - Adds Redis/cache tests for explicit fallback switching, local TTL expiry, and queue drop telemetry.
  - Adds WebSocket tests for degraded fallback bookkeeping, shutdown cancellation, and health semantics.
  - Adds AI/OpenAI tests for shared-session reuse, cache pruning, robust parsing, and cache-key correctness across distinct inputs.
  - Updates engine/command coverage where construction and command behavior changed.

items.title: Added 2nd question(Nash matrix)
items.body:
New features:

- A question generator for normal-form games with random payoffs (matrices between 2x2 and 10x10).
- Automatic computation of all pure Nash equilibria for each generated instance.
- Question formulation where the user must decide whether a pure Nash equilibrium exists and, if so, select a valid equilibrium position.
- Frontend display of the payoff matrix.
- Radio buttons for "Does a pure Nash equilibrium exist? Yes / No".
- Cell selection by clicking, with visual effects (hover, highlight, smooth animations).
- Disabling cell selection when the user chooses "No".
- Hidden input fields for sending the selected coordinates to the backend.
- 100% evaluation → correct answer (any valid Nash equilibrium is accepted if multiple exist).
- 0% evaluation → incorrect answer (wrong cell selection or mismatch with Yes/No).
- Results page updated to show the matrix, the user’s answer, the correct answer, and the score.

items.title: [API] Allow setting model name for `LMDeployWrapper`
items.body:
- Some VLMs like Phi-4-multimodal use [vision LoRA adapter](https://huggingface.co/microsoft/Phi-4-multimodal-instruct/tree/main/vision-lora) for vision tasks. However, current `LMDeployWrapper` can only always set `model` as base model automatically, causing incorrect evaluation results.
- This PR exposes `model` for `LMDeployWrapper` so that users can configure model name and send LoRA requests during evaluation to get correct responses.

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.14...v8.4.15)

#### 🌟 Summary (single-line synopsis)

Ultralytics **v8.4.15** improves real-world image ingestion (adds **HEIC/HEIF + HEIF** support with lazy decoding + better EXIF handling) and includes several quality fixes for metrics, exports, and docs 🖼️⚙️✅

#### 📊 Key Changes

- **HEIC/HEIF image support (priority change)** 🖼️📱
  - Added `ultralytics.utils.patches.image_open` and **monkey-patched `PIL.Image.open`** to lazily enable HEIC/HEIF decoding via **`pi-heif` only when needed** (i.e., on first decode failure) ⏱️
  - Expanded supported extensions to include **`.heif`** (in addition to `.heic`) ✅
  - Removed HEIC-specific loading code from dataset loaders (now unified through the standard image reading pathway) 🧹
- **Better plotting for non‑Latin text** 🈶🖋️
  - Improves matplotlib defaults by prioritizing **Arial Unicode MS** and auto-registering `.ttf` fonts from the Ultralytics user config directory for stronger multilingual rendering.
- **EXIF auto-rotation fix for list-of-path sources** 🔄🖼️
  - Applies `ImageOps.exif_transpose()` when loading images from **lists of paths/URLs**, reducing “sideways phone photo” issues.
- **Validation/metrics correctness fix (important for accuracy reporting)** 🎯📈
  - Fixes SciPy-based matching (`match_predictions`) to **maximize IoU** during assignment (previously could choose the worst matches), which can affect TP/FP classification and **mAP when `use_scipy=True`**.
- **IMX (Sony IMX500) export improvements** 📦🤖
  - **Enables IMX export on Linux ARM64** (removes an ARM64 block), adds dependency support, and improves test gating.
  - Adds **segmentation** as a supported IMX export/benchmark task ✅
- **Usability improvement: `Results.save()`** 💾📁
  - Adds `create_dir` parameter (default `True`) to control auto-creation of parent directories when saving annotated outputs.
- **Dev/CI reliability updates** 🧪🏗️
  - CI now tests newer PyTorch versions (2.8/2.9) and makes export tests less flaky by skipping TFLite export tests unless `torch>=1.13` on Linux.

#### 🎯 Purpose & Impact

- **More “it just works” image input** 🖼️✅
  - HEIC/HEIF (common on iPhones) can be used directly for training/inference with fewer manual conversions, while lazy loading avoids paying the dependency cost unless you actually need it.
- **Fewer confusing orientation bugs** 📱➡️🖥️
  - EXIF transpose handling reduces rotated/sideways images that can break visualization, training data review, and inference outputs.
- **More trustworthy evaluation metrics** 📈🧠
  - The IoU matching fix ensures SciPy-based evaluation behaves as intended, preventing artificially worse results or incorrect TP/FP assignment when that path is enabled.
- **Better edge/export support on ARM** 🧩🚀
  - IMX export on ARM64 + segmentation support expands deployment options for embedded and edge workflows.
- **Smoother workflows & sharing outputs** 💾✨
  - `Results.save(create_dir=True)` makes saving predictions into new folders simpler (fewer “directory not found” errors).
- **Improved global documentation and plots** 🈶📚
  - Better multilingual font defaults help teams with non‑Latin labels produce clearer charts/figures.

If you’re deploying/training with mixed photo sources (phones, HEIC libraries, multilingual labels), **8.4.15** is a practical upgrade 🛠️🚀

items.title: fix: correct proxy context path for expression evaluation
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes critical bug in proxy-wrapped `.get()` results where incorrect context paths caused expression evaluation, parent references, and scoped variable lookups to fail.

**Status**: All 330 tests now pass ✅ (was 13 failures)

## Problem

When commit 7ea54d3 introduced proxy wrapping for `.get()` results, it passed the wrong context path to the expression evaluator:
- **Incorrect**: Full path including the property being evaluated (e.g., `['user', 'name']` when evaluating `user.name`)
- **Correct**: Path to the container object (e.g., `['user']` when evaluating properties inside `user`)

This caused:
- Expression variables like `${firstName}` to resolve from wrong context
- Parent references (`..property`) to calculate paths incorrectly
- Scoped `.get()`, `.set()`, `.has()` methods to use wrong paths
- Proxy property descriptors to conflict with the empty target

## Solution

### Core Fixes

1. **Expression evaluation context** - Now excludes the property being evaluated
   ```typescript
   // Context for evaluating expressions in 'user.name'
   const pathArray = targetPath.split('.').filter(Boolean).slice(0, -1);
   // Result: ['user'] (correct container)
   ```

2. **Proxy wrapping** - Now includes the full path for scoped methods
   ```typescript
   // Path for proxy-wrapped 'user' object
   const pathArray = actualPath.split('.').filter(Boolean);
   // Result: ['user'] (enables user.get('name') to work)
   ```

3. **Proxy target** - Now uses actual data instead of empty object/array
   ```typescript
   const target = actualData;  // Not {} or []
   // Prevents property descriptor conflicts
   ```

4. **Parent reference calculation** - Restored correct formula
   ```typescript
   const baseSegments = parentSegments.slice(0, availableLevels - parentLevels);
   // Uses availableLevels, not parentSegments.length
   ```

### Additional Improvements

- Simplified scoped-proxy by removing unnecessary `ownKeys` and `getOwnPropertyDescriptor` traps
- All arrays (including primitive arrays) now consistently wrapped in proxies
- Error messages now show correct context path (container, not property)

## Testing

Added 18 comprehensive tests covering:
- ✅ Parent references with multiple levels (`..` and `...`)
- ✅ Array operations (indexing, spread, chaining, negative indexing)
- ✅ Complex template literals with backtick syntax
- ✅ Method chaining on expression results
- ✅ Built-in resolvers (Date, Math)
- ✅ Complex real-world patterns
- ✅ Advanced error handling

## Commits

1. **fix: correct proxy context path for expression evaluation** - Core bug fixes
2. **test: add comprehensive tests for advanced jsön features** - 18 new tests
3. **chore: refactor .claude and .specify workflow structure** - Dev workflow improvements
4. **docs: update README and build configuration** - Documentation updates
5. **chore: archive deprecated workflow files** - Move old files to .archive/

## Impact

- ✅ No breaking changes
- ✅ All 330 tests passing
- ✅ Proxy behavior matches original design intent
- ✅ Fixes issues from commit 7ea54d3

## Changeset

A patch changeset has been included documenting this bug fix.

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.14...v8.4.15)

#### 🌟 Summary (single-line synopsis)

Ultralytics **v8.4.15** improves real-world image ingestion (adds **HEIC/HEIF + HEIF** support with lazy decoding + better EXIF handling) and includes several quality fixes for metrics, exports, and docs 🖼️⚙️✅

#### 📊 Key Changes

- **HEIC/HEIF image support (priority change)** 🖼️📱
  - Added `ultralytics.utils.patches.image_open` and **monkey-patched `PIL.Image.open`** to lazily enable HEIC/HEIF decoding via **`pi-heif` only when needed** (i.e., on first decode failure) ⏱️
  - Expanded supported extensions to include **`.heif`** (in addition to `.heic`) ✅
  - Removed HEIC-specific loading code from dataset loaders (now unified through the standard image reading pathway) 🧹
- **Better plotting for non‑Latin text** 🈶🖋️
  - Improves matplotlib defaults by prioritizing **Arial Unicode MS** and auto-registering `.ttf` fonts from the Ultralytics user config directory for stronger multilingual rendering.
- **EXIF auto-rotation fix for list-of-path sources** 🔄🖼️
  - Applies `ImageOps.exif_transpose()` when loading images from **lists of paths/URLs**, reducing “sideways phone photo” issues.
- **Validation/metrics correctness fix (important for accuracy reporting)** 🎯📈
  - Fixes SciPy-based matching (`match_predictions`) to **maximize IoU** during assignment (previously could choose the worst matches), which can affect TP/FP classification and **mAP when `use_scipy=True`**.
- **IMX (Sony IMX500) export improvements** 📦🤖
  - **Enables IMX export on Linux ARM64** (removes an ARM64 block), adds dependency support, and improves test gating.
  - Adds **segmentation** as a supported IMX export/benchmark task ✅
- **Usability improvement: `Results.save()`** 💾📁
  - Adds `create_dir` parameter (default `True`) to control auto-creation of parent directories when saving annotated outputs.
- **Dev/CI reliability updates** 🧪🏗️
  - CI now tests newer PyTorch versions (2.8/2.9) and makes export tests less flaky by skipping TFLite export tests unless `torch>=1.13` on Linux.

#### 🎯 Purpose & Impact

- **More “it just works” image input** 🖼️✅
  - HEIC/HEIF (common on iPhones) can be used directly for training/inference with fewer manual conversions, while lazy loading avoids paying the dependency cost unless you actually need it.
- **Fewer confusing orientation bugs** 📱➡️🖥️
  - EXIF transpose handling reduces rotated/sideways images that can break visualization, training data review, and inference outputs.
- **More trustworthy evaluation metrics** 📈🧠
  - The IoU matching fix ensures SciPy-based evaluation behaves as intended, preventing artificially worse results or incorrect TP/FP assignment when that path is enabled.
- **Better edge/export support on ARM** 🧩🚀
  - IMX export on ARM64 + segmentation support expands deployment options for embedded and edge workflows.
- **Smoother workflows & sharing outputs** 💾✨
  - `Results.save(create_dir=True)` makes saving predictions into new folders simpler (fewer “directory not found” errors).
- **Improved global documentation and plots** 🈶📚
  - Better multilingual font defaults help teams with non‑Latin labels produce clearer charts/figures.

If you’re deploying/training with mixed photo sources (phones, HEIC libraries, multilingual labels), **8.4.15** is a practical upgrade 🛠️🚀

items.title: Implement complete lane-based note reading game system with strict melody and chord modes
items.body:
This PR implements a comprehensive lane-based note reading game system that transforms the existing game into a precisely controlled, multi-lane experience with strict melody evaluation and advanced chord recognition capabilities.

## Overview

The implementation adds a sophisticated lane management system that supports both Normal Mode (single lane) and Piano Mode (dual lanes with MIDI routing). Each lane operates independently with its own queue, lives, timing, and evaluation logic.

## Key Features

### Lane System Architecture

The system introduces three types of lanes:
- **Normal Mode**: Single `mono` lane handles all input
- **Piano Mode**: Dual lanes with precise MIDI routing
  - `bass` lane: MIDI ≤ 59 (B3 and below)  
  - `treble` lane: MIDI ≥ 60 (C4 and above)

### Strict Melody Mode

Implements strict note evaluation where any incorrect note press results in immediate target failure:
- Wrong note presses instantly blow up the active target
- Target queue advances after each evaluation
- Lives are decremented per failed attempt
- Each lane evaluates independently in Piano Mode

### Advanced Chord Recognition

Adds sophisticated chord mode with precise timing requirements:
- **100ms Collection Window**: All chord tones must be pressed within 100ms of the first correct tone
- **Stray Note Detection**: Any non-chord note causes immediate chord failure
- **Timeout Handling**: Incomplete chords automatically fail after the window expires
- **Duplicate Tolerance**: Already-collected chord tones are ignored

### MIDI Integration

Perfect integration with the existing Piano Mode infrastructure:
- Seamless MIDI device routing to appropriate lanes
- No cross-credit between bass and treble lanes
- Maintains backward compatibility with existing input system
- Automatic lane initialization on Piano Mode activation

## Technical Implementation

### Core Constants
```typescript
const BASS_MAX_MIDI = 59;        // B3
const TREBLE_MIN_MIDI = 60;      // C4
const CHORD_WINDOW_MS = 100;     // milliseconds  
const CHORD_SPAWN_MULTIPLIER = 1.25; // 25% slower chord spawning
```

### File Structure
- `src/midi/lane-system.ts` - Core lane state management and evaluation logic
- `src/midi/midi-integration.ts` - MIDI input routing and Piano Mode integration
- `script.js` - Game loop integration and lane system initialization
- `game.html` - Module loading updates for TypeScript components
- `tests/` - Comprehensive validation test suite

### Game Flow Integration

The lane system integrates seamlessly with the existing game loop:
1. MIDI input is routed to the appropriate lane based on note pitch
2. Each lane evaluates input against its active target independently  
3. Success/failure effects are triggered per lane
4. Visual updates and scoring occur through existing UI systems
5. Game over occurs when all lanes are disabled (lives ≤ 0)

## Screenshots

![Initial Game State](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5db9b7d3-99ea-401f-ba93-20f9ab352f86)

*Normal mode showing the game running successfully with single treble clef staff*

![Grand Staff Piano Mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa6afca8-1483-4131-805d-fb46576836b1)

*Piano Mode with Grand Staff showing the dual-lane system - notes appearing on both treble (top) and bass (bottom) staves with independent collision lines*

## Validation & Testing

All specified acceptance criteria have been implemented and verified:

✅ **Normal Mode Strict**: E-F-G queue, pressing F first → E blows up, F becomes active  
✅ **Piano Chord Stray**: Bass chord + treble melody, wrong bass note → bass fails, treble unaffected  
✅ **Piano Treble Strict**: Wrong treble note → treble target fails immediately  
✅ **Chord Window**: 100ms collection window with timeout failure  
✅ **MIDI Routing**: Precise ≤59/≥60 routing with no cross-credit  
✅ **Movement Speed**: Constant per lane, difficulty via spawn cadence only

The implementation includes a comprehensive test suite that validates all core functionality and boundary conditions with 100% pass rate.

## Backward Compatibility

This implementation maintains full backward compatibility:
- Existing Piano Mode UI and controls work unchanged
- Current MIDI device integration continues to function
- Legacy input methods (keyboard, touch) remain functional  
- All existing game features and modes are preserved

The changes are surgical and focused, adding the lane-based system as an enhancement layer while preserving all existing functionality.

### [`v8.4.18`](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/releases/tag/v8.4.18): - `ultralytics 8.4.18` `safe_download()` URLs with spaces (#​23736)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.17...v8.4.18)

#### 🌟 Summary

Ultralytics `v8.4.18` is a reliability-focused release that improves downloads and dependency installs, while also adding stronger ExecuTorch export support (including Pose) for smoother edge/mobile deployment 🚀.

#### 📊 Key Changes

- **🔧 Priority fix (current PR): `safe_download()` now handles URLs with spaces** by encoding spaces as `%20` (PR [#​23736](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/issues/23736) by [@​glenn-jocher](https://redirect.github.com/glenn-jocher)).
  - Prevents broken downloads from links like file paths or hosted assets containing spaces.
- **📱 Major export upgrade: ExecuTorch refactor + first-class utility module** (PR [#​23734](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/issues/23734) by [@​lakshanthad](https://redirect.github.com/lakshanthad)).
  - New `ultralytics/utils/export/executorch.py` with reusable `torch2executorch()` and `executorch_wrapper()`.
  - Export pipeline now uses this shared utility.
  - Added Pose-safe decoding patch for better XNNPACK compatibility.
  - Benchmarks no longer block Pose + ExecuTorch inference.
  - New reference docs page for ExecuTorch export.
- **📦 Dependency handling improvement for `git+` requirements with version constraints** (PR [#​23737](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/issues/23737) by [@​fcakyon](https://redirect.github.com/fcakyon)).
  - Fixes invalid install behavior by cleaning git URL requirement strings before install.
- **📒 Notebook/API modernization** (PR [#​23745](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/issues/23745) by [@​ahmet-f-gumustas](https://redirect.github.com/ahmet-f-gumustas)).
  - Object tracking notebook updated from deprecated `Annotator.seg_bbox()` to modern `Results.plot(color_mode="instance")`.
- **📚 Docs updates**
  - OBB docs now point to a newer YOLO26 tutorial video (PR [#​23738](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/issues/23738) by [@​RizwanMunawar](https://redirect.github.com/RizwanMunawar)).
  - Vercel Web Analytics added to docs site template for usage insights (PR [#​23746](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/issues/23746) by [@​glenn-jocher](https://redirect.github.com/glenn-jocher)).

#### 🎯 Purpose & Impact

- **More reliable downloads for everyone** ✅\
  The `safe_download()` fix is small but high-impact: fewer random failures when fetching models/assets from imperfect URLs.
- **Better edge deployment path** 📲\
  ExecuTorch export is now cleaner, more maintainable, and better for Pose workflows—helpful for teams deploying YOLO26 on mobile/embedded targets.
- **Fewer setup headaches** 🧩\
  Git-based dependency auto-update now works more as users expect, reducing installation friction in custom environments.
- **Examples stay working and easier to follow** 🎥\
  Notebook/API updates reduce breakage from old methods and keep learning materials aligned with current Ultralytics usage.
- **Docs quality can improve faster over time** 📈\
  Analytics and refreshed tutorials help the team prioritize what users need most.

#### What's Changed

- Add version constraint support for git URL requirements by [@​fcakyon](https://redirect.github.com/fcakyon) in [#​23737](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/23737)
- Refactor ExecuTorch export to `executorch.py` by [@​lakshanthad](https://redirect.github.com/lakshanthad) in [#​23734](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/23734)
- Fix outdated `Annotator.seg_bbox` in object tracking notebook by [@​ahmet-f-gumustas](https://redirect.github.com/ahmet-f-gumustas) in [#​23745](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/23745)
- Add <https://youtu.be/128JhhR2DlM> to docs by [@​RizwanMunawar](https://redirect.github.com/RizwanMunawar) in [#​23738](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/23738)
- Docs analytics by [@​glenn-jocher](https://redirect.github.com/glenn-jocher) in [#​23746](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/23746)
- `ultralytics 8.4.18` `safe_download()` URLs with spaces by [@​glenn-jocher](https://redirect.github.com/glenn-jocher) in [#​23736](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/23736)

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.17...v8.4.18>

### [`v8.4.17`](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/releases/tag/v8.4.17): - `ultralytics 8.4.17` NDJSON dataset re-split support (#​23735)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.16...v8.4.17)

#### 🌟 Summary (single-line synopsis)

Ultralytics **v8.4.17** makes NDJSON dataset conversions *resplit-friendly*—reusing existing images, cleaning stale labels, and avoiding unnecessary downloads for faster iteration 🚀📦

#### 📊 Key Changes

- **NDJSON dataset re-split support (priority change)** ♻️🧹
  - Detects when the dataset output folder already exists and **reuses previously downloaded images** when you change `train/val/test` splits.
  - For non-classification tasks (detect/segment/pose), **removes the existing `labels/` directory** before reconversion to prevent stale annotations.
  - If an image is missing from the current split, it will **move (rename) it from another split** (train/val/test) *before* downloading from the URL.
  - Adds a **content hash** (ignoring signed/rotating URLs) stored in `data.yaml` to **skip reconversion when nothing meaningful changed** 🧾🔒
  - **Deletes orphaned images** that are no longer part of the dataset after a resplit, reducing “stale background files” that can silently affect training 🗑️
- **More reliable EdgeTPU exports** 🧩⚙️
  - Automatically **disables `end2end` mode for EdgeTPU** exports (and logs a warning), aligning EdgeTPU with other limited backends that don’t support required ops.
- **OpenVINO INT8 export dependency handling improved** 📦✅
  - Adds PyTorch **2.3 detection** and adjusts `nncf` requirements to reduce install/export conflicts across Torch versions.
- **Clearer disk space error messages** 💾🔎
  - Fixes incorrect “GB” reporting and now shows **MB for sizes under 1GB**, making download/asset errors easier to understand.

#### 🎯 Purpose & Impact

- **Faster dataset iteration for NDJSON workflows** ⚡\
  Resplitting a dataset no longer forces full re-downloads—saving time, bandwidth, and friction when you’re refining splits during curation.
- **Fewer training gotchas from stale files** 🧼\
  Clearing old labels and removing orphaned images helps prevent subtle mismatches (images/labels out of sync) that can degrade training quality.
- **More dependable deployment exports** 📤\
  EdgeTPU exports should fail less often due to unsupported `end2end` behavior, and OpenVINO INT8 export setups are smoother across PyTorch versions.
- **Better user experience when storage is low** 🧰\
  Disk space errors now communicate real numbers, reducing confusion during downloads and conversions.

#### What's Changed

- Fix incorrect disk space in error message by [@​Y-T-G](https://redirect.github.com/Y-T-G) in [#​23727](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/23727)
- Pin `nncf<3` for PyTorch 2.2 and below by [@​Y-T-G](https://redirect.github.com/Y-T-G) in [#​23726](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/23726)
- Disable `end2end` for EdgeTPU by [@​Y-T-G](https://redirect.github.com/Y-T-G) in [#​23724](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/23724)
- `ultralytics 8.4.17` NDJSON dataset re-split support by [@​glenn-jocher](https://redirect.github.com/glenn-jocher) in [#​23735](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/23735)

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.16...v8.4.17>

### [`v8.4.16`](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/releases/tag/v8.4.16): - `ultralytics 8.4.16` Windows<>Linux model compatibility fix (#​23725)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.15...v8.4.16)

#### 🌟 Summary (single-line synopsis)

Ultralytics **8.4.16** mainly improves **Windows ↔ Linux/macOS `.pt` model portability** by fixing `pathlib` pickle issues, with a small docs update for **HEIC/HEIF** image support 🧩💾📸

#### 📊 Key Changes

- 🪟🖥️ **Cross-platform `.pt` loading fix (PR [#​23725](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/issues/23725) by [@​glenn-jocher](https://redirect.github.com/glenn-jocher)):**
  - Updated `torch_safe_load()` to **remap `pathlib.WindowsPath` ↔ `pathlib.PosixPath`** during unpickling, preventing common load failures when models are created on one OS and loaded on another.
- 🧵 **Checkpoint metadata made safer/more consistent:**
  - `model.pt_path` is now stored as a **plain string** (`str(weight)`), not a `Path` object (applies in general checkpoint loading and YOLO NAS model wrapper code).
- 🔢 **Version bump:** `8.4.15` → `8.4.16`.
- 📸 **Docs + format clarity (PR [#​23717](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/issues/23717)):**
  - Docs now reflect that **HEIC/HEIF uses `pi-heif` (auto-installed on first use)** and **AVIF is supported natively by Pillow**.
  - `.heif` is explicitly listed among supported image formats.

#### 🎯 Purpose & Impact

- ✅ **Fewer “can’t unpickle WindowsPath/PosixPath” errors** when sharing trained `.pt` weights between teammates or CI systems running different operating systems.
- 🔁 **More reliable export and tooling workflows** that depend on `model.pt_path` (strings behave consistently across platforms and serialization).
- 👥 **Better collaboration & reproducibility** for teams training on Linux servers and deploying/testing on Windows machines (or vice versa).
- 📸 **Smoother HEIC/HEIF user experience** thanks to clearer docs and explicit `.heif` support visibility (less dependency confusion).

#### What's Changed

- Update HEIC/HEIF dependency info and add .heif format to docs by [@​raimbekovm](https://redirect.github.com/raimbekovm) in [#​23717](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/23717)
- `ultralytics 8.4.16` Windows<>Linux model compatibility fix by [@​glenn-jocher](https://redirect.github.com/glenn-jocher) in [#​23725](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/23725)

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.15...v8.4.16>

### [`v8.4.15`](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/releases/tag/v8.4.15): - `ultralytics 8.4.15` HEIC/HEIF image support (#​23714)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.14...v8.4.15)

#### 🌟 Summary (single-line synopsis)

Ultralytics **v8.4.15** improves real-world image ingestion (adds **HEIC/HEIF + HEIF** support with lazy decoding + better EXIF handling) and includes several quality fixes for metrics, exports, and docs 🖼️⚙️✅

#### 📊 Key Changes

- **HEIC/HEIF image support (priority change)** 🖼️📱
  - Added `ultralytics.utils.patches.image_open` and **monkey-patched `PIL.Image.open`** to lazily enable HEIC/HEIF decoding via **`pi-heif` only when needed** (i.e., on first decode failure) ⏱️
  - Expanded supported extensions to include **`.heif`** (in addition to `.heic`) ✅
  - Removed HEIC-specific loading code from dataset loaders (now unified through the standard image reading pathway) 🧹
- **Better plotting for non‑Latin text** 🈶🖋️
  - Improves matplotlib defaults by prioritizing **Arial Unicode MS** and auto-registering `.ttf` fonts from the Ultralytics user config directory for stronger multilingual rendering.
- **EXIF auto-rotation fix for list-of-path sources** 🔄🖼️
  - Applies `ImageOps.exif_transpose()` when loading images from **lists of paths/URLs**, reducing “sideways phone photo” issues.
- **Validation/metrics correctness fix (important for accuracy reporting)** 🎯📈
  - Fixes SciPy-based matching (`match_predictions`) to **maximize IoU** during assignment (previously could choose the worst matches), which can affect TP/FP classification and **mAP when `use_scipy=True`**.
- **IMX (Sony IMX500) export improvements** 📦🤖
  - **Enables IMX export on Linux ARM64** (removes an ARM64 block), adds dependency support, and improves test gating.
  - Adds **segmentation** as a supported IMX export/benchmark task ✅
- **Usability improvement: `Results.save()`** 💾📁
  - Adds `create_dir` parameter (default `True`) to control auto-creation of parent directories when saving annotated outputs.
- **Dev/CI reliability updates** 🧪🏗️
  - CI now tests newer PyTorch versions (2.8/2.9) and makes export tests less flaky by skipping TFLite export tests unless `torch>=1.13` on Linux.

#### 🎯 Purpose & Impact

- **More “it just works” image input** 🖼️✅
  - HEIC/HEIF (common on iPhones) can be used directly for training/inference with fewer manual conversions, while lazy loading avoids paying the dependency cost unless you actually need it.
- **Fewer confusing orientation bugs** 📱➡️🖥️
  - EXIF transpose handling reduces rotated/sideways images that can break visualization, training data review, and inference outputs.
- **More trustworthy evaluation metrics** 📈🧠
  - The IoU matching fix ensures SciPy-based evaluation behaves as intended, preventing artificially worse results or incorrect TP/FP assignment when that path is enabled.
- **Better edge/export support on ARM** 🧩🚀
  - IMX export on ARM64 + segmentation support expands deployment options for embedded and edge workflows.
- **Smoother workflows & sharing outputs** 💾✨
  - `Results.save(create_dir=True)` makes saving predictions into new folders simpler (fewer “directory not found” errors).
- **Improved global documentation and plots** 🈶📚
  - Better multilingual font defaults help teams with non‑Latin labels produce clearer charts/figures.

If you’re deploying/training with mixed photo sources (phones, HEIC libraries, multilingual labels), **8.4.15** is a practical upgrade 🛠️🚀
